subject: Private offer packaging: usage vs bundled SKUs and partner margin trace
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Barnes <emma@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private offer packaging: usage vs bundled SKUs and partner margin trace

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, I wanted to capture the two packaging options we discussed for the private offer and a quick ask on partner margin visibility so your finance team can run the passback. High level:

- Option A: Usage-first SKUs (metered node-hours + embeddings) — lower list price, predictable unit economics for you, easier for your teams to scale up/down.
- Option B: Bundled (Reserved nodes + monthly support + embeddings) — higher upfront commitment, clearer SKU on the marketplace, simplifies internal invoicing.

Can you confirm which approach your procurement prefers? If they go with Option B (bundled), they typically need a line-item for partner commission so they can route the passback to resellers; if Option A they usually want evidence of historical usage smoothing to justify the usage floors.

Attached is a first draft pricing matrix (CB_Pricing_Matrix_v2.xlsx) that shows both builds and our suggested list price vs. private-offer net. Also attached is a working draft of the private offer term sheet.

Next steps I propose: 1) you share a short list of internal PO questions from procurement, 2) if you prefer Option B we can produce a marketplace-friendly SKU mapping for Azure/GCP, and 3) Ben (cc) will run through partner margin traces with your channel contact if needed.

Thanks —
Camila
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CB_Pricing_Matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_privoffer_draft_v3.pdf (term sheet)

From: Emma Barnes <emma@cloudbridge.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private offer packaging: usage vs bundled SKUs and partner margin trace

Hi Camila —

Appreciate the clear summary and matrix — this is helpful. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement and our channel team: 

1) If we pick Option B (bundled), will the marketplace SKU need to be listed as a single line item or can the reserved nodes + support be two line items under one private offer?
2) For Option A, can you share the 6-month usage smoothing file so our FP&A can model the proposed usage floors?
3) Our reseller (CloudResell) requires the commission path to be included in the invoice metadata so passbacks are automatic. What fields do you emit in the marketplace invoice?

Also looping in Azure Marketplace Ops (mp-ops@azuremarketplace.com) for any SKU naming rules. If you can respond with a recommended implementation (single SKU vs multi-line SKU) and the sample usage smoothing CSV, we can move to procurement questions.

Best,
Emma
Head of Cloud Partnerships
CloudBridge

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 11:22:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Private offer packaging: usage vs bundled SKUs and partner margin trace

Camila / Lauren —

Forwarding Emma's procurement questions. Quick internal notes / suggested answers before we send a formal reply: 

- SKU line items on Azure/GCP: Marketplace allows both single-line private offers and multi-line attachments. For customer simplicity we recommend a single bundled SKU that represents the committed package; internally we itemize components in the invoice metadata (this satisfies CloudResell's passback).

- Usage smoothing: I'll export the 6-month rolling node-hour CSV (anonymized) and include a recommended floor at the 60th percentile of observed usage. That gives them headroom and avoids overcommitment.

- Invoice metadata: we emit the following fields currently: sku_id, private_offer_id, partner_passback_code, reseller_id, list_price, net_price, usage_hours (when metered). We can add an explicit reseller_commission_percent field if CloudResell needs it.

Action items for Lauren: can you draft a short marketplace SKU naming suggestion for Azure (name + mkt-sku id + short description) and confirm which metadata keys we can bake into the invoice payload? I can attach the anonymized usage CSV once ready.

Ben
Sr. Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private offer packaging: usage vs bundled SKUs and partner margin trace

Emma —

Thanks — quick updates and deliverables attached.

1) Marketplace SKU recommendation (attached in the matrix tab): we propose a single marketplace SKU for the bundled private offer: 
   - SKU display name: Redwood CloudBridge Reserved Pack (Azure)
   - internal mkt_sku: RDW-CB-RSV-AZ-1
   - invoice metadata: sku_id, private_offer_id, partner_passback_code, reseller_id, reseller_commission_pct, list_price_usd, net_price_usd

2) Usage smoothing: attached anonymized 6-month CSV as requested. Our recommendation: floor = 60th percentile; we included a sample calculation in the matrix.

3) Partner margin trace: we will add reseller_commission_pct to the invoice metadata and provide CloudResell with the passback code. That should allow automatic commission routing on your side.

Next steps: if procurement confirms Option B, I can kick off the private offer creation and route to Azure for listing. If they prefer Option A, we'll send a metered private-offer build and include the usage-floor clause in the terms.

Attaching: CB_Pricing_Matrix_v2.xlsx (updated with SKU names), usage_smoothing_6mo.csv (anonymized), redwood_privoffer_draft_v3.pdf

Cheers,
Camila
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CB_Pricing_Matrix_v2.xlsx, usage_smoothing_6mo.csv, redwood_privoffer_draft_v3.pdf
